title: C4-C4 incident-energy dependence of EOS moving-nucleon neutral-current scattering
physical_validation_status: not a transport or literature-reproduction acceptance
energy_grid_note: The six-point grid is an exploratory first-pass choice, not a final physical boundary or a user-approved exclusion range.

kernel.definition: Gamma_N^avail(E,r)=2*pi*integral[-1,1] dcos(theta) integral[Eprime_min,Eprime_max] dEprime dGamma_N/(dEprime dOmegaprime)
kernel.support: Exact p_min(Eprime,cos(theta);mstar)<=p_max with the existing 45*T momentum-tail cutoff; roots are recomputed for each energy, radius, target and angular node.
kernel.opacity: kappa_N=xi_SPP*Gamma_N^avail; xi_SPP is applied exactly once.
kernel.mean_free_path: lambda_N=1/kappa_N, converted from MeV^-1 to km using hbar*c=197.3269804 MeV fm.
kernel.local_energy_convention: Fixed local incident energy at each sampled radius; no gravitational redshift or energy redistribution.

interpretation: The output is a four-radius local total-scattering energy scan, not a 301-radius opacity or optical-depth calculation.
The 100-MeV entries are reused byte-provenanced C4-C2 reference values and are not recomputed.
The C4-C3 100-MeV 301-radius flat-space diagnostic remains the baseline and is not replaced.
No transport, escape probability, redshift, hydrodynamic feedback, or supernova exclusion is inferred.
The scan is not a physical validation of the pure-vector Blinov Fig. 7 benchmark.
